summary:
S. 4745, introduced in the 119th Congress, is a single-section bill that designates a specific United States Postal Service facility. The primary purpose of the legislation is to rename the postal facility located at 201 East Grant Avenue in Georgetown, Ohio, as the "Ulysses S. Grant Post Office Building." 

Section 1(a) establishes this designation as a matter of federal law. Section 1(b) contains a conformity provision directing that any reference to the specified facility in any federal law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States shall be deemed a reference to the "Ulysses S. Grant Post Office Building." 

The bill does not amend the United States Code, create new regulatory authority, repeal existing statutes, authorize appropriations, or establish any conditions precedent, exceptions, or specific effective dates.
